## **Homophones and Allomorphs**
<br>
<table style="width:100%; border-collapse:collapse">
  <tr>
    <td style="width:1%; text-align:center;"></td>
    <td style="width:10%; text-align:center; border:3px solid orange; background-color:#FFF176"><h3><span style="color:black;"><b>homophones</b></span></h3></td>
    <td style="width:1%; text-align:center;"><span style="color:white">-</span></td>
    <td style="width:40%; text-align:left; border:3px solid orange">
    <ul>
      <li>
        sound the same, but mean different things<br><br>
        <ul>
          <li>
            <i>small-er → <span style="color:orange">-er</span></i> = <span style="color:orange">'more'</span>&nbsp&nbsp&nbsp&nbsp&nbsp&nbsp&nbsp&nbsp
            <i>help-er → <span style="color:orange">-er</span></i> = <span style="color:orange">'agent'</span>
          </li>
          <li>
            <i>paper-s → <span style="color:orange">-s</span></i> = <span style="color:orange">PLURAL</span>&nbsp&nbsp&nbsp&nbsp&nbsp&nbsp
            <i>see-s → <span style="color:orange">-s</span></i> = <span style="color:orange">3SG PRESENT</span>
          </li>
        </ul>
      </li><br>
      <li>
        these are <span style="color:orange"><b>different morphemes</b></span> that happen to sound the same
      </li><br>
      <li>
        <span style="color:orange"><b>homophonous</b></span> not <span style="color:orange"><b>homophobous</b></span>
      </li>
    </ul>
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td style="width:1%; text-align:center;"></td>
    <td style="width:10%; text-align:center;"><span style="color:white">-</span></td>
    <td style="width:1%; text-align:center;"><span style="color:white">-</span></td>
    <td style="width:40%; text-align:center;"><span style="color:white">-</span></td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td style="width:1%; text-align:center;"></td>
    <td style="width:10%; text-align:center; border:3px solid blue; background-color:#A4C2F4"><h3><span style="color:black"><b>allomorphs</b></span></h3></td>
    <td style="width:1%; text-align:center;"><span style="color:white">-</span></td>
    <td style="width:40%; text-align:left; border:3px solid blue">
    <ul>
      <li>
      mean the same thing, but are pronounced differently<br><br>
        <ul class="two-col-grid">
          <li>
            <i>wug<span style="color:blue">-s</span></i>,
            <i>peff<span style="color:blue">-s</span></i>,
            <i>gutch<span style="color:blue">-es</span></i>&nbsp&nbsp&nbsp&nbsp&nbsp&nbsp&nbsp&nbsp
            <i>talk<span style="color:blue">-ed</span></i>,
            <i>buzz<span style="color:blue">-ed</span></i>,
            <i>land<span style="color:blue">-ed</span></i>
          </li>
          <li>
            <i><span style="color:blue">magic</span>-al</i>,
            <i><span style="color:blue">magic</span>-ian</i>&nbsp&nbsp&nbsp&nbsp&nbsp&nbsp&nbsp&nbsp&nbsp&nbsp&nbsp&nbsp&nbsp&nbsp
            <i><span style="color:blue">clear</span>-ing</i>,
            <i><span style="color:blue">clar</span>-ify</i>
          </li>
        </ul>
      </li><br>
      <li>
        each of these is a <span style="color:blue"><b>separate morpheme</b></span> with multiple pronunciations and each pronunciation is called an <span style="color:blue"><b>allomorph</b></span> of that morpheme
      </li>
    </ul>
    </td>
  </tr>
</table>

## **Types of Morphemes I: Free vs. Bound**
<br>
compare two **lexical entries** we have seen:
<br><br>
.pull-left[
<table style="width:100%; border-collapse:collapse;">
  <tr>
    <td style="width:15%; text-align:center; border:1px solid black;">label</td>
    <td style="width:15%; text-align:center; border:1px solid black;"><span style="color:#CC0033">'dog'</span></td>
    <td style="width:15%; text-align:center; border:1px solid black;"><span style="color:#CC0033">'teach'</span></td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td style="width:15%; text-align:center; border:1px solid black;"><b>phonological representation</b></td>
    <td style="width:15%; text-align:center; border:1px solid black;">/dɑg/</td>
    <td style="width:15%; text-align:center; border:1px solid black;">/tiːtʃ/</td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td style="width:15%; text-align:center; border:1px solid black;"><b>semantic representation</b></td>
    <td style="width:15%; text-align:center; border:1px solid black;">{x: x is a <i><b><span style="color:green">dog</span></b></i>}</td>
    <td style="width:15%; text-align:center; border:1px solid black;">{&lt;x, y&gt;: x <i><b><span style="color:green">teaches</span></b></i> y}</td>
  </tr>
</table>
]

.pull-right[
<table style="width:100%; border-collapse:collapse;">
  <tr>
    <td style="width:15%; text-align:center; border:1px solid black;">label</td>
    <td style="width:15%; text-align:center; border:1px solid black;"><span style="color:#CC0033">'-er'</span></td>
    <td style="width:15%; text-align:center; border:1px solid black;"><span style="color:#CC0033">'-able'</span></td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td style="width:15%; text-align:center; border:1px solid black;"><b>phonological representation</b></td>
    <td style="width:15%; text-align:center; border:1px solid black;">/ər/</td>
    <td style="width:15%; text-align:center; border:1px solid black;">/əbəl/</td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td style="width:15%; text-align:center; border:1px solid black;"><b>semantic representation</b></td>
    <td style="width:15%; text-align:center; border:1px solid black;">one who does <i><b><span style="color:orange">X</span></b></i> action</td>
    <td style="width:15%; text-align:center; border:1px solid black;">able to be<br><i><b><span style="color:orange">X</span></b></i>-ed</td>
  </tr>
</table>
]
<br>

.pull-left[
<div style="text-align:center">
  <h2><b>
    <span style="color:#CC0033">free morpheme</span>
  </b></h2>
  can stand alone as a word<br>
  e.g. <i>dog</i>, <i>cat</i>, <i>house</i>,
</div>
]
.pull-right[
<div style="text-align:center">
  <h2><b>
    <span style="color:green">bound morpheme</span>
  </b></h2>
  cannot stand alone<br>
  e.g. <i>-er</i>, <i>-s</i>, <i>cran-</i>
</div>
]

<div style="text-align:center">
  <h3><b>
    <span style="color:orange">-infix-</span>
  </b></h3>
</div>
<table style="width:100%; border-collapse:collapse">
  <tr>
    <td style="width:15%; text-align:center;"><h3><span style="color:#FF1778">prefix-</span></h3></td>
    <td style="width:15%; text-align:center; border:3px solid blue"><h3><span style="color:#C7CCD4">root(s)</span></h3></td>
    <td style="width:15%; text-align:center;"><h3><span style="color:#00DBB2">-suffix</span></h3></td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td style="width:15%; text-align:center;"><h3><span style="color:brown">circum-</span></h3></td>
    <td style="width:15%; text-align:center;"></td>
    <td style="width:15%; text-align:center;"><h3><span style="color:brown">-fix</span></h3></td>
  </tr>
</table>

## **Types of Morpheme II: Root vs. Affixes**
<br>
<table style="width:100%; border-collapse:collapse">
  <tr>
    <td style="width:1%; text-align:center;"></td>
    <td style="width:10%; text-align:center; border:3px solid #CC0033; background-color:#FF8686"><h3><span style="color:black;"><b>root</b></span></h3></td>
    <td style="width:1%; text-align:center;"><span style="color:white">-</span></td>
    <td style="width:40%; text-align:left; border:3px solid #CC0033">
    <ul>
      <li><span style="color:#CC0033"><b>"base"</b></span> morpheme to which other morphemes are attached</li><br>
      <li>contributes the <span style="color:#CC0033"><b>core meaning</b></span> of the word</li><br>
      <li>if a word has a single morpheme, that morpheme is a root</li><br>
      <li>examples: <i><span style="color:#CC0033">danc</span>-ing</i>, <i>dis-<span style="color:#CC0033">appear</span></i>, <i><span style="color:#CC0033">help</span>-less-ness</i>, <i><span style="color:#CC0033">elephant</span></i></li><br>
    </ul>
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td style="width:1%; text-align:center;"></td>
    <td style="width:10%; text-align:center;"><span style="color:white">-</span></td>
    <td style="width:1%; text-align:center;"><span style="color:white">-</span></td>
    <td style="width:40%; text-align:center;"><span style="color:white">-</span></td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td style="width:1%; text-align:center;"></td>
    <td style="width:10%; text-align:center; border:3px solid green; background-color:#62D095"><h3><span style="color:black"><b>affix</b></span></h3></td>
    <td style="width:1%; text-align:center;"><span style="color:white">-</span></td>
    <td style="width:40%; text-align:left; border:3px solid green">
    <ul>
      <li>morpheme that is <span style="color:green"><b>attached to the root</b></span></li><br>
      <li><span style="color:green"><b>prefixes</b></span> go before root, <span style="color:green"><b>suffixes</b></span> go after root – both are affixest</li><br>
      <li>a word can have multiple prefixes or suffixes</li><br>
      <li>Examples: <i><span style="color:green">in-</span>complete</i>, <i>act<span style="color:green">-ive</span></i>, <i><span style="color:green">un-</span>trust<span style="color:green">-worthy</span></i>, <i><span style="color:green">will</span>-ing-ly</i></li><br>
    </ul>
    </td>
  </tr>
</table>

---
## **Types of Morphemes III**
### **Inflectional vs. Derivational**
<br>
<table style="width:100%; border-collapse:collapse">
  <tr>
    <td style="width:1%; text-align:center;"></td>
    <td style="width:10%; text-align:center; border:3px solid green; background-color:#62D095"><h3><span style="color:black"><b>inflextional</b></span></h3></td>
    <td style="width:1%; text-align:center;"><span style="color:white">-</span></td>
    <td style="width:40%; text-align:left; border:3px solid green">
    <ul>
      <li><span style="color:green"><b>inflectional morphemes</b></span> are used to <b>inflect</b> words</li><br>
      <li>they add grammatical nuance but do not change the core meaning</li><br>
      <li>in English, they’re mostly used to conjugate verbs (<i>jump</i> → <i>jump<span style="color:green">-ed</span></i>), pluralize nouns (<i>cat</i> → <i>cat<span style="color:green">-s</span></i>), and form the comparative and superlative
of adjectives (<i>bright</i> → <i>bright<span style="color:green">-er</span></i> → <i>bright<span style="color:green">-est</span></i>)</li>
    </ul>
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td style="width:1%; text-align:center;"></td>
    <td style="width:10%; text-align:center;"><span style="color:white">-</span></td>
    <td style="width:1%; text-align:center;"><span style="color:white">-</span></td>
    <td style="width:40%; text-align:center;"><span style="color:white">-</span></td>
  </tr>

  <tr>
    <td style="width:1%; text-align:center;"></td>
    <td style="width:10%; text-align:center; border:3px solid #CC0033; background-color:#FF8686"><h3><span style="color:black;"><b>derivational</b></span></h3></td>
    <td style="width:1%; text-align:center;"><span style="color:white">-</span></td>
    <td style="width:40%; text-align:left; border:3px solid #CC0033">
    <ul>
      <li><span style="color:#CC0033"><b>derivational morphemes</b></span> are used to derive <span style="color:#CC0033">new words</b></span></li><br>
      <li>they change the core meaning of the word in some way</li><br>
      <li>they can, but do not always, change a word's part of speech<br><br>
        <ul>
          <li>
            <i>simple</i> → <i>simpl<span style="color:#CC0033">-ify</span></i>,
            <i>exist</i> → <i>exist<span style="color:#CC0033">-ence</span></i>,
            <i>pack</i> → <i><span style="color:#CC0033">un-</span>pack</i>
          </li>
        </ul>
      </li>
    </ul>
    </td>
  </tr>
</table>

## **Why Order Matters**
<br>
.pull-left[
consider words below **morphemes** make them up
  - unusable
  - unlockable
]

--

.pull-right[
<br>
  - **un-**<b>us(e)<span style="color:green">-able</span></b>
  - **un-**<b>lock<span style="color:green">-able</span></b>
]<br><br>

--
<h3><span style="color:#CC0033"><b>what are possible meanings of these two adjectives?</b></span></h3>

<br>
.pull-left[
- **un-**<b>us<span style="color:green">-able</span></b> has <b>only one meaning</b>
  - not able to be used
- **un-**<b>lock<span style="color:green">-able</span></b> is on the other hand, <b>ambiguous</b>
  - not able to be locked
  - able to be unlocked
]

.pull-right[
### Semantic Gap
]

### **why are they different though both are formed by attaching the same morphemes to the root?**

## **Affixes are 'Picky'**
<br>
.pull-left[<br><img src="../pic/0916/headache.jpg" width="85%">]
.pull-right[
affixes have **selectional requirements**, meaning that they can only attach to
stems of **a particular category**:<br><br>
- **inflectional** affix:<br><br>
  - comparative ***–er*** attaches only to adjectives<br>
  *tall-<b>er</b>*, \* *cat-<b>er*</b><br>
  - plural ***–s*** attaches only to nouns<br>
  *cat-<b>s</b>*, \* *tall-<b>s</b>*<br><br>
- **derivational** affix:<br><br>
  - ***re-*** attaches only to verbs<br>
  *<b>re</b>-do*, *<b>re</b>-visit*, \* *<b>re</b>-red*, \* *<b>re</b>-pencil*
]

---
## **Affixes are 'Picky'**
<br>
.pull-left[<br><img src="../pic/0916/headache.jpg" width="85%">]
.pull-right[
- in addition to being picky about their base, **derivational** affixes also **determine**
the category of the resulting word:<br><br>
  - derivational ***-ness*** attaches to adjectives to create nouns<br>
  *loneli-<b>ness</b>*, *happi-<b>ness</b>*, *concrete-<b>ness</b>*<br><br>
  - derivational ***-able*** attaches to verbs to create adjectives<br>
  *search-<b>able</b>*, *plan-<b>able</b>*, *do-<b>able</b>*<br><br>
- affixes can be even pickier, only attaching to certain types of nouns<br><br>
  - the derivational affix ***-ion*** attaches to verbs of only **Latin** origin to
create nouns<br>
  - *convers-<b>ion</b>*
]

]

## **Back to Order of Affixation**
<br>
.pull-left[
the **selectional restrictions** of affixes often help us **determine** the order in which
they were attached<br><br>
- consider the following polymorphemic word<br><br>
  - <i>**re**-<b>play-<span style="color:green">able</span></b></i><br><br>
- which affix was attached **first** to the root *<b>play</b>*?
]
.pull-right[<img src="../pic/0916/morphosyn.jpg" width="65%">]<br><br><br><br>

--

- ***re-*** has to be attached first, since it cannot attach to adjectives <br><br>
  - *<b>play</b>* → <i>**re**-<b>play</b></i> → <i>**re**-<b>play-<span style="color:green">able</span></b></i>

## **Morphological Structure**
<br>
.pull-left[
<div style="text-align:center">
<h3> 
<span style="color:#CC0033"><b>happy</b></span> + <span style="color:green"><b>-ly</b></span> = <span style="color:blue"><b>happily</b></span><br>
<span style="color:#CC0033"><b>crazy</b></span> + <span style="color:green"><b>-ly</b></span> = <span style="color:blue"><b>crazily</b></span><br>
<span style="color:#CC0033"><b>bright</b></span> + <span style="color:green"><b>-ly</b></span> = <span style="color:blue"><b>brightly</b></span>
</h3>
</div>
]
.pull-right[
<div style="text-align:center">
<h3> 
<span style="color:green"><b>un-</b></span> + <span style="color:#CC0033"><b>do</b></span> = <span style="color:blue"><b>undo</b></span><br>
<span style="color:green"><b>un-</b></span> + <span style="color:#CC0033"><b>real</b></span> = <span style="color:blue"><b>unreal</b></span><br>
<span style="color:white"><b>un- +</b></span><span style="color:white"><b> real =</b></span> <span style="color:white"><b>= undo</b></span>
</h3>
</div>
]
<br><br>

--

.pull-left[
<div style="text-align:center">
<h3>

## **Morphological Structure**
<br>
.pull-left[<br><br><img src="../pic/0916/puppet.jpg" width="90%">]
.pull-right[
- as we said, **order of affixation** affects the **meaning** of a word<br><br>
- the fact that we can't add affixes in any order suggests that words have a **hierarchical structure**<br><br>
- we can visualize this structure with a **tree diagram** as above<br><br>
- or an alternative is **labeled bracketing**, which is more compact but perhaps less intuitive:
<br><br>
<span style="color:red">[<sub>Adj</sub> un- </span><span style="color:green">[<sub>Adj</sub></span> <span style="color:blue">[<sub>V</sub> lock ]</span><span style="color:green"> -able ]</span> <span style="color:red">]</span>
<br><br>
<span style="color:red">[<sub>Adj</sub></span> <span style="color:green">[<sub>V</sub> un-</span><span style="color:blue"> [<sub>V</sub> lock ]</span> <span style="color:green">]</span><span style="color:red"> -able ]</span>

]
---
## **Morphological Tree Drawing**
### **de-humid-ify-er**
<br>
1. identify the word's morphemes and write them out separately in one row
2. identify the root (or roots) and label its **part of speech**
3. look at the morphemes immediately before and after the root<br>
  check **which one is added first**, draw lines upward connecting them, <br>
  and **label** the new words's part of speech
4. this new word becomes the base you'll keep building off of<br>
  **repeat step 3** using this new base<br><br>

## **Morphological Structure: Ambiguity**
<br><br>
.pull-left[
<br><br><br>
.pull-left[
*un* + *able*<br><br>
<img src="../pic/0916/undo3.png" width="90%">
]
.pull-right[
*undo* + *able*<br><br>
<img src="../pic/0916/undo4.png" width="90%">
]
]
.pull-right[
- the case of **unlockable** is an example of a word with an **ambiguous structure**<br><br>
- depending on the structure you assign it, it has a **different meaning**<br><br>
- both meanings are acceptable <br><br>
- which means the **meaning** of words is directly affected by their morphological structure<br><br>
- that's why **structure** is important, without knowing the structure, we would not be able to be **compositional** properly
]

## **Note 2: Ungrammaticality**
<br><br>
### <b>sometimes neither order works: \* *enjoyful*</b>
<br>
- **-ful**: N → Adj
- **en-**: N → V
<br><br><br>
<div style="text-align:center">
<h3><b><span style="color:blue">en</span><span style="color:green">joy</span> + ful</b> ❌</h3><br>
<h3><b>en +<span style="color:green">joy</span><span style="color:orange">ful</span></b> ❌<h3>
</div>

---
## **Note 3: Comparing Analysis**
<br><br>
### <b>sometimes both orders seem working — but not really</b>
<br>
- **-able**: V → Adj: <span style="color:orange">wash-able</span>, <span style="color:orange">do-able</span>
- **re-**: V → V, but NOT V → Adj: \* <span style="color:orange">re-big</span>, \* <span style="color:orange">re-sad</span>
<br><br>
<div style="text-align:center">
<h3><b><span style="color:blue">re-</span><span style="color:green">wash</span><span style="color:orange">-able</span></b>
</div>
.pull-left[<img src="../pic/0916/rewashable1.png" width="80%">]
.pull-right[<img src="../pic/0916/rewashable2.png" width="80%">]
